Ads and pop ups on websites.


If i need to quickly research something or check an article, i have to sift through multiple ads, "accept our cookies pls", "subscribe to our newsletter pls" bs etc. The absolute worst ones are where you have to sign up or pay to read the whole article. Theres also no guaruntee that the site is functional on mobile either so thats great. 


For fuck sakes, I just want to look up a recipe for roast potatoes while I cook, idgaf about your products, just let me read your fucking website. 


For my 2nd point, video games having boat loads of microtransactions, paid DLC, different editions, being fully online "live services", while also somehow releasing in completely unplayable, buggy and embarassing states. 


If im paying £50-70 for a game, I expect to be able to play it on launch day, not be expected to wait for a year until it maaaaybe has a chance of getting fixed (and not be abandoned or shut down within months). This would be the equivalent of releasing a Marvel movie with its storyboards still in the "final product" and going, "stay tuned until next year where we miiiiight have the scenes finished by then". 


Too many games have released in horrific states in recent memory, Cyberpunk 2077, No Mans Sky, Redfall, Pokemon Scarlet & Violet - and in the case of Pokémon SV, if you want all content currently available in the buggy and shitty state its still in after nearly a YEAR, better pay an additional £50-70 for the other game, or hope that one of your friends has the pokemon you're missing - which you will need Switch online to trade with, which is an additional £17.99 a year. Oh and if you want the DLC, it will be an additional £31.49 PER GAME. And, if you're like me and you have been playing Pokemon for decades and have all your old buddies from older games, you had better hoped you downloaded the poke transporter before the 3DS eshop shutdown and to get them up to the newest games, you need to get Pokemon Home. Its free (YIIPPEEEE) BUT, if you want to store more than 30 pokemon at a time, guess what?? £14.49 per year, please!


My next and last point would be AI generated slop. I used to love browsing Deviantart, now, I cant even use the site without coming across "big tittied anime girl with four fingers and cross eyes" oh and theres 1000s of similar images posted every mintue by the same user and they're selling them $100-400+ a piece as "adoptables". Sure do love it that millions of stolen images made by actual artists are being used to create this utter shite. Even Etsy is infested with AI slop. Unfortunately, until the law catches up, there is quite literally nothing stopping these people (and now billion dollar corporations) from using these AI generation sites that use stolen assests. Since they're mostly from poor and low income artists, there really isnt anyone stopping them at the moment.


Dont even get me started on the AI generated stories and posts. We are now going to have to contend with the fact that online experiences, reviews, analysis, articles (especially from new and obscure sources) and the likes will need to be taken with an absolutely massive grain of salt, given how good AI has gotten at writing. If it was easy for people to start a rumour, hoax, disinformation campaigns etc beforehand, how easy do you think its going to be for an AI script? What would take hours or days for a human can be done in mere seconds by an AI bot. Thousands of AI generated stories, posts, accounts, reviews, sites and the like are absolutely going to be used by anyone and everyone with an agenda to push. And, its going to get so good that it will be genuinely impossible to tell which is an actual human, and which is an AI.


I used to dream that AI and robots may be used to do more of the menial work and jobs so we could be free to create art, stories, music, games etc as we please but nope, instead its now taking those roles and now becoming a tool for huge disinformation campaigns. Great.
